readme: Memory evaluation corpus. Categories mirror LongMemEval so results are comparable to the published literature. The load-bearing category is `knowledge_update`: each item seeds a fact, then a later fact that supersedes it, and asks a question whose only correct answer is the newer one. A memory system that cannot represent supersession will return both, and the `stale` field is what detects that — the published failure rate for naive retrieval is 15-40%, and cosine similarity cannot distinguish a contradiction from a duplicate (AUROC 0.59, i.e. chance). `seed` entries are written in order, so a later entry genuinely arrives after an earlier one. `keys` is the `subject|relation` claim key MEMORY_EXTRACTION_INSTRUCTIONS asks the model to return for each seed, and it is the one thing this harness has to supply in the model's place. Two seeds share a key exactly when they are two values of one claim; seeds that state different claims about the same subject (a holiday and a return date) carry different keys, which is what makes an over-eager supersession show up here as a recall drop rather than passing unnoticed.
